entities.name: Maximilian of Lorch
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Saint Maximilian of Lorch or Saint Maximilian of Celeia was a Catholic bishop and missionary in the Roman province of Noricum. He was born around 245 AD and martyred in AD 288.

As a prominent figure in the early Christian Church, Maximilian played a crucial role in spreading Christianity throughout the Roman Empire. His missionary work in Noricum, a province that spanned modern-day Austria, Germany, and parts of Italy, helped to establish Christianity as a significant force in the region.

The martyrdom of Saint Maximilian of Lorch in 288 AD had a profound impact on the Christian community in Noricum, inspiring countless others to follow in his footsteps and spread the teachings of Jesus Christ. His legacy can still be seen in the many churches and monasteries that bear his name, testifying to the enduring power of his faith.

One striking statistic about Saint Maximilian of Lorch is that he was one of the earliest Christian martyrs, and his martyrdom was celebrated by the early Christian Church as a symbol of faith and perseverance.

In conclusion, the life and legacy of Saint Maximilian of Lorch serve as a powerful reminder of the importance of faith, perseverance, and the spread of Christianity throughout the ancient world.
